title: Sophisticated Lady and the $15 check
summary: He and Otto Hardwick supplied the first eight bars and release, and each got a $15 check that cancelled any composer credit.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You hadn't been in the band very long a tune called "Sophisticated Lady" was recorded, and I find it rather interesting that in Benny Ashland's discography, which was published in Scandanavia, that on February 15th, 1933, you hadn't been in the band even a year then, there was a recording session at which "Sophisticated Lady" was recorded. And Ashland lists the composers as Ellington, Hardwick, Brown and Mills. I notice on record labels that that isn't the list at all. They say Ellington, Mills and Parish. Who wrote "Sophisticated Lady".

Well, that's one of those everybody jumps in and helps out, but mainly I had a theme which I played all the time which is the first eight bars. And Otto Hardwick played the -- the release, and I went back to the first eight bars. That was the basic tune of "Sophisticated Lady". And I got the terrific check of $15.00 for -- for writing "Sophisticated Lady"
Wow. Now -- have you ever gotten co-composer credits?

No. No. That check cancels you out. See, no one knew what was going to happen. You never know when you have a good coming number on your hands, so -- in fact, we didn't even care. We just was doing something that we wanted to do.
Did Otto get a check too?
Yeah, he and I both. I know that because I saw it.
Gee. That was quite a bargain, wasn't it?
That happened on some of the other tunes in the band, didn't it?
Quite a few. Yes, quite a few.
